title: First-order least-squares FEM and practical DPG

items.title: Planar rotation carries H(div) normal traces to tangential traces
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For a nondegenerate oriented triangle $K\subset\mathbb R^2$, set $R(a,b)=(-b,a)$, let $n$ be cell-outward and $t=Rn$. If $\sigma\in H(\operatorname{div};K)$ is real, then $R\sigma\in H(\operatorname{curl};K)$, $\operatorname{curl}(R\sigma)=\operatorname{div}\sigma$ distributionally, and $\int_K(R\sigma\cdot R\nabla\phi+\operatorname{curl}(R\sigma)\phi)=\langle\gamma_n\sigma,[\phi]\rangle$ for all $\phi\in H^1(K)$. Thus weak tangential trace equals weak normal trace under $t=Rn$.

Here $H(\operatorname{curl};K):=\{w\in L^2(K;\mathbb R^2):\partial_1w_2-\partial_2w_1\in L^2(K)\}$ with its graph norm. The weak tangential trace is the functional on $H^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ defined by the integral in the Statement; the computation below proves it is the rotation of the PE08 weak normal trace.
items.strategy: Define the two-dimensional rotated H(curl) interface locally from the actual H(div) trace supplier; verify the distributional derivative identity and orientation sign without importing the 3D PE09 trace Statement.

items.title: First-order least-squares formulation of the Dirichlet Poisson problem
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be bounded connected Lipschitz and $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Solve $-\Delta u=f$, $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$; set $\sigma=-\nabla u$, so $\operatorname{div}\sigma=f$. For a finite conforming shape-regular triangular mesh, define $X_h=RT_0(\mathcal T_h)\times(P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega))$ and $J_h(\sigma_h,u_h)=\|\sigma_h+\nabla u_h\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}\sigma_h-f\|_2^2$. Here $RT_0(K)=P_0(K)^2+xP_0(K)$ and $P_1$ is continuous piecewise affine. The real Sobolev-space and zero-boundary conventions are [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; H(div), mesh, and RT conventions are [[def-na-hdiv-space]] and [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. This is the plan-spec PE30 sign convention; negating the design flux converts its residuals to these and preserves the squared objective. Integrals are exact; geometry, quadrature and roundoff errors are excluded.
items.strategy: State the real spaces, load, sign convention, mesh, conforming RT0/P1 trial family, and squared residual functional; the proof suppliers establish conformity and norm equivalence separately.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be bounded connected Lipschitz and $C_P$ satisfy $\|w\|_2\le C_P\|
abla w\|_2$ on $H^1_0$. For $z=(\delta\sigma,\delta u)\in H(div)	imes H^1_0$, put $Rz=(\delta\sigma+
abla\delta u,div\delta\sigma)$. This is injective and its norm is equivalent to the product graph norm. If $a=\|R_1z\|_2$, $b=\|R_2z\|_2$, $g=\|
abla\delta u\|_2$, then $g\le a+C_Pb$, $\|\delta u\|_2\le C_P(a+C_Pb)$, $\|\delta\sigma\|_2\le2a+C_Pb$, and $\|Rz\|^2\le2\|z\|^2_{H(div)	imes H^1}$.

items.title: Exact local finite Riesz solves for practical DPG tests
items.statement:
**Inputs:** A finite-dimensional real graph-test space presented as $V_r(K)=\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_N\}$, an ordered finite generating family (not assumed independent), a trial datum $w$, the graph inner product $(\cdot,\cdot)_V$, and the linear functional $\ell_w(v)=b_K(w,v)$ on $V_r(K)$.

**Output:** Either a vector in $V_r(K)$ or the status `singular-test-matrix`.

**Admissible conditions:** $N\ge0$; all entries are real and exact; $\ell_w$ is defined and linear on $V_r(K)$. The Gram entries and functional values are evaluated exactly. No quadrature or rounded solve is part of this procedure.

**Instructions:**

1. Form $G_{ij}=(v_j,v_i)_V$ and $g_i=\ell_w(v_i)$ exactly.
2. Initialize $L=I_N$ and compute an unpivoted symmetric $LDL^{\mathsf T}$ factorization in the listed order. At pivot $k$, set
   $$d_k=G_{kk}-\sum_{j<k}L_{kj}^2d_j.$$
   If $d_k\le0$, return `singular-test-matrix`. Otherwise set $D_{kk}=d_k$ and
   $$L_{ik}=\frac{G_{ik}-\sum_{j<k}L_{ij}L_{kj}d_j}{d_k}\qquad(i>k).$$
3. Solve $Lz=g$, $Dy=z$, and $L^{\mathsf T}c=y$ exactly, and return $\sum_{j=1}^N c_jv_j$. For $N=0$, return the zero vector of $V_r(K)$.
items.strategy: Specify inputs, exact output tests, element-local Gram systems, an exact positive-definiteness check, and the failure status; numerical quadrature and floating solve errors are not included.

items.title: Weak H(div) normal trace surjects onto the scalar trace dual
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the local trace quotient convention of [[lem-na-hdiv-weak-normal-trace]]. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open; all spaces are real. With $T_D=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D)$ and its quotient norm, the weak normal trace map
$$\gamma_n:H(\operatorname{div};D)\longrightarrow T_D',\qquad \langle\gamma_n\tau,[w]\rangle=\int_D\bigl(\tau\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}\tau)w\bigr),$$
is onto. In fact every $L\in T_D'$ has a lift $\tau\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$ satisfying $\gamma_n\tau=L$ and $\|\tau\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le\|L\|_{T_D'}$.
items.strategy: Represent a scalar trace-dual functional on H1 by Riesz; its vanishing on H1_0 forces the Riesz vector to solve Delta z=z distributionally, so grad z is H(div) and its weak normal trace is the original functional.

items.title: Ultraweak Poisson skeleton spaces are Hilbert trace quotients
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. The elementwise trace map $\Gamma_0:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\prod_KH^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ and normal-trace map $\Gamma_n:H(div;\Omega)\to\prod_K(H^1(K)/H^1_0(K))'$ have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift infimum norms. These equal the infima over broken extensions whose gluing belongs to the respective global space. Compatibility means membership in these ranges, so normal traces are conservative on each interior facet in the weak distributional sense.
items.strategy: Prove trace-map continuity and closed kernels, identify range norms with quotient norms, and prove the scalar and normal-trace gluing implications by elementwise Green identities and facet cancellation.

items.title: Ideal Poisson DPG trial-to-test Riesz map
items.statement:
**Input:** A real trial vector $w\in U$.

**Output:** The ideal test vector $Tw\in V$.

**Admissible conditions:** $U$ and $V$ are the real Hilbert spaces in [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]], and $b$ is the bounded real bilinear form on them, with boundedness supplied by [[lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-bilinear-form-bounded]]. The definition uses exact Hilbert-space operations and makes no claim of practical computability.

**Instructions:** Form the bounded linear functional $\ell_w(v)=b(w,v)$ on $V$. Apply the Hilbert-space Riesz representation procedure to obtain the unique $Tw\in V$ satisfying
$$
(Tw,v)_V=\ell_w(v)=b(w,v)\qquad(v\in V),
$$
and return $Tw$. For a finite-dimensional trial subspace $U_h$, the ideal test space is $T(U_h)$.
items.strategy: Specify the bounded functional on the real Hilbert test space, invoke the exact published Riesz hypotheses, and define the ideal test space without claiming its computability.

The exact functional $J_h$ has a unique minimizer in the conforming RT0/P1 family, and that minimizer is the orthogonal best approximation in the residual inner product. Its scalar component remains in $H^1_0(\Omega)$.

items.title: A topology-free bounded lifting of every ultraweak Poisson load
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the real spaces and signs of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. For every bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedron $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, and every finite conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh, give $U$ the squared product norm from its two $L^2$ factors and two global trace lift-infimum norms, and give $V$ its full broken graph norm. Define $B:U\to V'$ by $(Bx)(y)=b(x,y)$. There is a bounded linear map $R:V'\to U$ such that $BR=I_{V'}$ and $\|R\|\le C_*$. Choose any $C_P>0$ with $\|w\|_2\le C_P\|\nabla w\|_2$ for $w\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, put $a=(C_P^2+2)^{1/2}$, and set $$C_*^2=(1+a)^2+(1+C_Pa)^2+(1+C_P^2)a^2+(\sqrt2+a)^2+1.$$ The constant is independent of the mesh. No simple-connectivity or connected-boundary hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy: Represent an arbitrary broken graph-dual load by its exact four-coefficient Riesz vector, solve one global H1_0 variational problem, form a global H(div) field with the required divergence, use its actual traces, verify all five signed pairings, and sum the product-norm bounds.

items.title: Fortin stability and quasi-optimality for practical DPG
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the real form and spaces of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]] on a finite conforming triangular mesh. For every admissible local input to [[alg-na-practical-dpg-finite-riesz-solves]], the exact factorization terminates after $O(N_K^3)$ scalar arithmetic operations once its Gram entries and right-hand side are formed; it returns `singular-test-matrix` exactly for a dependent input family, and on an independent family it returns the unique finite Riesz representative. Let $U_h\subset U$ consist of volume fields $\sigma_h|_K\in P_1(K)^2$, $u_h|_K\in P_1(K)$, continuous scalar traces $\widehat u_h|_{\partial K}\in\widetilde P_2(\partial K)$, and conservative normal traces $\widehat\sigma_{n,h}|_{\partial K}\in P_1(\partial K)$. This is finite-dimensional. Let $V_r=\prod_K(P_3(K)^2\times P_3(K))$, presented cellwise by fixed ordered bases, and let $T_r:U_h\to V_r$ be the assembled finite Riesz map. On each fixed basis the unique local Riesz representatives assemble to a bounded linear map satisfying $\|T_rw_h\|_V\le\|b\|\|w_h\|_U$. Now assume the continuous primal and adjoint graph inf-sup constants have minimum $\beta>0$. Let $\Pi:V\to V_r$ be the bounded Fortin map of [[lem-na-practical-dpg-fortin-p1-r3]], with $b(U_h,(I-\Pi)V)=0$ and $\|\Pi\|\le C_\Pi$. Then for every bounded load $F\in V'$, the practical DPG system tested with $T_r(U_h)$ has a unique solution $x_h$, and
$$\|x-x_h\|_U\le(1+\|b\|C_\Pi/\beta)\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U,$$
where $x$ is the exact continuous solution.
items.strategy: Derive the discrete inf-sup bound from the explicit Fortin identities, express the practical DPG equations as the mixed residual Riesz system, apply the exact Babuška–Brezzi supplier, and prove the quasi-optimal estimate.

items.title: Adjoint graph inf-sup for ultraweak Poisson on connected Lipschitz polyhedra
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For every bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedron $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, and every finite conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh, give $U$ its $L^2$/global-quotient product norm and $V$ the full broken graph norm of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. With $C_*$ from [[lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-bounded-load-lifting]], the primal and adjoint bounds are $$\sup_{y\ne0}\frac{|b(x,y)|}{\|y\|_V}\ge C_*^{-1}\|x\|_U,\qquad \sup_{x\ne0}\frac{|b(x,y)|}{\|x\|_U}\ge C_*^{-1}\|y\|_V.$$ Both constants are independent of the mesh. The bounded operator $B:U\to V'$ and its Riesz trial-to-test map $T:U\to V$ are boundedly invertible, with inverse norms at most $C_*$. No simple-connectivity or connected-boundary hypothesis is required; connected polyhedra with holes are included.
items.strategy: Use the global arbitrary-load right inverse to obtain surjectivity, combine it with the proved zero trial kernel for bounded invertibility and the primal bound, and use the Hilbert Riesz map to construct an adjoint witness for each test vector.

items.title: Ideal ultraweak Poisson DPG is the energy best approximation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the real trial/test spaces and bilinear form of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]], with $|b(w,v)|\le5\|w\|_U\|v\|_V$ as in [[lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-bilinear-form-bounded]]. The ideal trial-to-test map $T$ of [[alg-na-ultraweak-poisson-ideal-trial-to-test]] is well defined, bounded linear, and satisfies $\|T\|\le5$. Let $x\in U$ be any exact ultraweak solution and let $U_h\subset U$ be finite dimensional. The ideal DPG equations with test space $T(U_h)$ have a unique solution $x_h$, which is the orthogonal projection of $x$ in the induced energy inner product $(w,z)_E=(Tw,Tz)_V$. Consequently $\|x-x_h\|_E=\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_E=\|B(x-x_h)\|_{V'}$.
items.strategy: The trivial trial kernel makes the Riesz trial-to-test map injective; its image inner product is the energy inner product, and finite-dimensional orthogonal projection gives existence, uniqueness, best approximation, and the residual identity.

items.title: Practical DPG residual is reliable and efficient up to data oscillation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Assume the continuous trial-to-test operator is boundedly invertible with lower inf-sup constant $\beta>0$, and let $\Pi:V\to V_r$ be the bounded Fortin map with $b(U_h,(I-\Pi)V)=0$. For any exact solution $x=B^{-1}F$ and any $\widetilde x_h\in U_h$, define the practical residual estimator $\eta=\|F-B\widetilde x_h\|_{V_r'}$ and Fortin data oscillation $\operatorname{osc}(F)=\|F\circ(I-\Pi)\|_{V'}$. Then
$$\beta^2\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U^2\le\eta^2+(\|\Pi\|\eta+\operatorname{osc}(F))^2,\quad \eta\le\|b\|\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U,$$
$$\operatorname{osc}(F)\le\|b\|\|I-\Pi\|\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U.$$
For the stated P1/R3 Poisson Fortin map, $\operatorname{osc}(F_f)\le C(\sum_Kh_K^2\|f-f_K\|_{L^2(K)}^2)^{1/2}$, where $f_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K f$; it vanishes for cellwise constant $f$.
items.strategy: Prove the full residual-representer reliability identity by orthogonal projection onto the discrete test space, use the Fortin property to bound the omitted component, derive efficiency from restriction of the full dual norm, and identify the Poisson data oscillation.

items.title: P1/R3 practical DPG quasi-optimality and residual estimator for Poisson
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be any bounded connected Lipschitz polygon, including polygons with holes, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be any finite conforming shape-regular triangular mesh. Use the exact two-dimensional P1/R3 practical family selected in PE30: volume fields $\sigma_h|_K\in P_1(K)^2$ and $u_h|_K\in P_1(K)$; compatible global scalar traces of degree at most two on facets, zero on boundary facets; conservative global normal traces of degree at most one; and broken tests $V_r=\prod_K(P_3(K)^2\times P_3(K))$, with the graph inner product inherited from $V$. The local Fortin projection $\Pi:V\to V_r$ is that of [[lem-na-practical-dpg-fortin-p1-r3]], and $C_\Pi$ is its operator norm bound. For each $f\in L^2(\Omega)$, the continuous ultraweak solution $x$ and practical solution $x_h$ exist uniquely, with $$\|x-x_h\|_U\le(1+5C_\Pi C_*)\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U.$$ For every $\widetilde x_h\in U_h$, put $\eta=\|F_f-B\widetilde x_h\|_{V_r'}$, where $V_r'$ is the dual of $V_r$ with its induced norm, and $\operatorname{osc}(F_f)=\|F_f\circ(I-\Pi)\|_{V'}$. Then $$C_*^{-2}\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U^2\le\eta^2+(C_\Pi\eta+\operatorname{osc}(F_f))^2,\qquad \eta\le5\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U,$$ and $$\operatorname{osc}(F_f)\le C_{\rm osc}\left(\sum_Kh_K^2\|f-f_K\|_{L^2(K)}^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad f_K=|K|^{-1}\int_Kf,$$ where $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and $C_{\rm osc}$ is the cellwise constant from the Fortin map's mean-preserving local $L^2$ estimate. The constants $C_*$, $C_\Pi$, and $C_{\rm osc}$ are independent of mesh size for the fixed domain and shape-regular family. The practical corollary is two-dimensional; the continuous graph theorem also covers dimension three.
items.strategy: Instantiate the locally proved connected-domain graph inf-sup theorem in dimension two, apply the exact P1/R3 Fortin map to the conditional practical and residual estimates, and use scalar cell-mean preservation for the data-oscillation bound.

title: First-order least-squares FEM and practical DPG — Examples

items.title: Dropping the H1-zero boundary condition makes least squares nonunique
items.statement: If zero boundary values are removed from the continuous first-order Poisson least-squares problem with zero load, every constant scalar $u$ with $\sigma=0$ has zero residual; hence the unconstrained minimizer is not unique.
items.strategy: Take f=0 and any nonzero constant; verify both residual components vanish and contrast with the actual H^1_0 boundary condition.

items.title: An exact polynomial Poisson solution has a zero residual certificate
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On $\Omega=(0,1)^2$ with its two-triangle diagonal mesh, let $u=x(1-x)y(1-y)$, $\sigma=-\nabla u$, and $f=-\Delta u$. Then $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, $\sigma\in H(div;\Omega)$, $\sigma+\nabla u=0$, and $div\sigma-f=0$, so the continuous least-squares residual is zero.
items.strategy: Differentiate the quartic polynomial, verify the four boundary restrictions, calculate div(-grad u)=-Delta u, and evaluate both squared residual terms.

items.statement: On one triangle, take a four-dimensional trial subspace of $P_1(K)^2\times P_0(K)$ and the three-dimensional constant test space $P_0(K)^2\times P_0(K)$. The practical trial-to-test map has a nontrivial kernel, so the normal equations cannot have a unique trial solution for any load for which a solution exists.
items.strategy: Compute the dimensions of P0(K)^2 x P0(K) and a four-vector trial subspace, then apply finite-dimensional rank-nullity to the Riesz trial-to-test map.

items.statement: Let $U=V=\mathbb R^2$ with Euclidean inner product, $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $b(x,y)=(Ax)\cdot y$, $U_h=\operatorname{span}(e_2)$, practical test space $V_r=\operatorname{span}(e_1)$, and load $F(y)=e_1\cdot y$. Then $Te_2=(1,1)$, $T^re_2=e_1$, and ideal and practical trial coefficients are $1/2$ and $1$.
items.strategy: Compute the two Riesz maps from the identity and one-dimensional Gram matrices, then solve the one-by-one ideal and practical Galerkin equations exactly.
